meta.title: Ondra Egress Gate
meta.description: Egress inventory, compliance notice, and a three-tier risk warning. It does not encrypt and it does not proxy: a proxy would have to carry the payload itself, which puts credential values into this package's memory, error contexts, and eventually the log, creating a second credential path that O-035 had just eliminated by redefining key injection as presence preflight plus reference registration. So it answers one question only: may this go out, where to, and who approved it. A capability declares what it sends, where, why it must leave the machine, and which environment variable it needs, then asks before sending; an undeclared capability is refused rather than allowed by default. The three tiers are separated by reversibility rather than adjectives: metadata or anonymous text is tier one notice, images, audio, files, identifiable data, or irreversible actions are tier two confirmation, and secret-shaped content, a credential written as a value, an undeclared host, or an unregistered capability is tier three block. The approval mode changes the disposition but never the tier, because letting full-auto relabel a high risk as low would erase the finding from the panel. Turning the gate off cancels notice and confirmation but never the red lines, since a red line that a switch can turn off is not a red line. Consent is remembered per capability and host and persisted, otherwise every start asks again and the third ask sends the user looking for the switch; a corrupt ledger reads as empty rather than as blanket consent; credentials are stored as variable names only; scan hits report offsets and kinds, never the text. No tool is registered, because consent is a human act and the model must not be able to nod on its own.
